problem: The lead states as a general property of the whole PBF family that 'overhangs need no separate support structure'. This is true for polymer SLS but false for metal PBF, where supports/anchors are needed for heat flow and to control warping. Section 2 corrects this, but a student reading only the lead will learn the wrong rule.
fix: Restrict the claim: 'In polymer SLS the unfused powder holds the next layer, so overhangs need no separate support. Metal PBF still needs support anchors for heat flow and to limit warping.'

problem: The platform is lowered twice: bullet 1 is 'Lower the build platform by one layer thickness' and bullet 6 is 'Lower the platform and repeat until all slices are built'. A student cannot tell whether lowering once or twice per layer is intended.
fix: Keep lowering as one step of the loop. Either drop the 'Lower the platform' words from bullet 6 and write 'Repeat from the spreading step until all slices are built', or remove bullet 1 and keep the lowering only after scanning.

problem: The chapter says DMLS 'fully melts' metal powder. Many textbooks and exam keys describe DMLS as liquid-phase sintering at the grain level and reserve full melting for SLM, so a student writing 'DMLS sinters' in an exam would appear to contradict this book.
fix: Add one line: 'The name DMLS comes from sintering, and older texts describe it as grain-level liquid-phase sintering; modern DMLS machines melt the powder fully, so here it is grouped with SLM.'

problem: Step 5 and the answer line both give 'about 6.94 h', repeating the same value twice with no new information.
fix: Write step 5 as: 'In hours: T = 25,000 / 3,600 = 6.94 h' and leave the answer line as 'The estimated laser scan time is 25,000 s, about 6.94 h; real build time is higher because recoating adds time.'
